newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast crudes gain, despite lower ANS deal.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast crudes gain, despite lower ANS deal.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crude prices firmed early Friday despite news that a cargo of Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude sold for a higher discount.
Overall, outright ANS prices rose about 10 cents to $21.35/21.65 a barrel amid a WTI spot market buoyed by strong heating oil futures.
Heating oil for October delivery was seen about 1.67 cents higher from Thursday, tracking a strong gas oil market on London's IPE.
But ANS gains were curbed somewhat by falling differentials.
A cargo for October delivery sold early Friday at Oct. WTI minus $2.15 a barrel. The last done deal sold at $2.05 off October.

Traders had forecast lower October deltas because of excess crude remaining from a high number of summer refinery outages. ANS production was also weighed by a seasonal rise following the end of summer maintenance programs in Alaska.
Values for Wilmington stood at $16.60/16.70 cents a gallon while Kern River remained $14.50/15.00 a barrel, after rising mid-week with posted prices.
Line 63 differentials were unchanged at WTI minus $2.60/2.50 a barrel, with little trading seen ahead of mid-September.
